newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS END LOWER ON WEAK MARKET SENTIMENT.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS END LOWER ON WEAK MARKET SENTIMENT.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower on Thursday after investors sold bank, finance and communication stocks, brokers said.
The composite SET index finished 4.04 points off at 628.69 on light 2.32 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index fell 0.37 to 47.56.
"The setbacks of bank, finance and some communication issues dragged down the key index. But the market was actually quiet," said one broker at United Securities.
Losers led gainers 170 to 72 with 61 closing unchanged.
Brokers said market sentiment remained weak on lingering worries about the economic downturn, finance sector crisis and volatility of regional currency markets.
Second-quarter results of some major listed companies did not move the market as their earnings were largely in line with market expectation, they said.
Bangkok Bank closed unchanged at 168 baht, and PTTEP rose four to 410 after it announced a 35 percent rise of its second quarter profit to 337 million baht.
